channel.title: The Hollywood Reporter Inc. - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Hollywood Reporter Inc. (thr.com)

item.title: ‘Give Me the Ball!’ Review: Rousing Bio-Doc Pays Tribute to the Indomitable Billie Jean King, Whose Tenacity Equalized the Professional Tennis Court
item.description: ESPN’s ‘30 for 30’ series entry, directed by Liz Garbus and Elizabeth Wolff, is a lovingly made account of the life and career of a galvanizing force in sports, women’s rights and LGBTQ visibility.

item.title: “Long Live Women in Music”: Chappell Roan, Chaka Khan, Joni Mitchell and More Gather for Resonator Awards
item.description: The star-studded event, put on by the organization We Are Moving the Needle, kicked off Grammy Week by gathering attendees for a celebration of women working in the music industry.

item.title: Odessa A’zion Pulls Out of A24 Film ‘Deep Cuts’ After Casting Backlash: “I Hadn’t Read the Book”
item.description: The ‘Marty Supreme’ and ‘I Love LA’ star has apologized to fans of the book and revealed that she voluntarily backed out of the film, which is supposed to start shooting in February.

item.title: ‘Four Minus Three,’ Premiering at Berlin, Is Based on a True Story of Family, Death, Grief, Hope – and Clowns (Exclusive Clip)
item.description: Adrian Goiginger's new feature, based on Barbara Pachl-Eberhart's bestselling book, stars Valerie Pachner and Robert Stadlober, and will debut in the Berlinale's Panorama section.

item.title: ‘Between Brothers’ Is a Deeply Personal Doc, Debuting at Rotterdam, That Takes Viewers on a Road Trip to Unravel Family Trauma and Mystery
item.description: In his new film, premiering at IFFR, Dutch writer-director Tom Fassaert follows his father and uncle as they look for signs of their long-lost father and explores the cycle of intergenerational trauma.

item.title: ‘Clueless,’ ‘The Karate Kid,’ ‘Glory,’ ‘The Big Chill,’ ‘High Society,’ ‘The Grand Budapest Hotel’ Enter the National Film Registry
item.description: Also picked for preservation: ‘The Thing,’ ‘Before Sunrise,’ ‘Frida,’ ‘Inception,’ ‘Philadelphia,’ ‘The Incredibles’ and ‘The Hours,’ while Ken Burns makes the list for the first time.

item.title: Berlin Adds Chinese Animation ‘Light Pillar’ to Perspectives Lineup
item.description: Xu Zao’s sci-fi feature is set in the distant future in a nearly deserted film studio.

item.title: Japan Box Office Roars Back to Record High in 2025, Powered by ‘Demon Slayer’ and ‘Kokuho’
item.description: Total ticket sales revenue jumped 32 percent to a record 274.45 billion yen ($1.79 billion) as local megahits drove the world’s third-largest film market past its prior pre-pandemic peak.

item.title: ‘Melania,’ the First Lady’s New Documentary, Abruptly Pulled From Release in South Africa
item.description: Melania Trump's film is still getting what's likely to be the widest release of all time at the global box office for a doc, including a revised location count of 1,778 locations in North America and as many as 3,000 cinemas globally.
